user_reported_bug: Refine the Budget Scenarios page and perform a global button contrast fix. Budget Scenarios: make the 'Adjusted What-If' column significantly more distinct from Baseline (highlight/double-border), use green/red indicators for numerical differences (savings=bold green, extra cost=sharp red), consistent in light+dark. Button contrast: no button same colour as its background; teal buttons use white/off-white text; clay backgrounds use a distinct shade/border (no clay-on-clay); all button text high-contrast/legible.
summary: No relevant testing skill found. Logged in as cathy@example.com on the preview URL and tested Budget Scenarios in light+dark, the dark dashboard/statement button and badge contrast cases, the AI disclaimer/Your Rights panel, and the legacy invoice-checker route. Several fixes pass (slider red/green deltas in both themes, Save scenario contrast, Complete now CTA, AI anomaly disclaimer, High/Medium/Low badges, and /app/tools/invoice-checker/list redirect), but the Budget Scenarios adjusted column is still not a readable clay-highlighted what-if column and dark mode still has flat/transparent primary buttons plus a Your Rights pill with 1.16:1 contrast.

ui_bugs.issue: Light mode: adjusted column uses transparent background/effective bg equal to page bg, neutral border rgb(231,223,213), blue ring, and the What-If badge is white text on transparent/warm bg with 1.06:1 contrast. It is not the requested clay highlight/double-border and the badge is barely visible.

Dark mode: adjusted column text is dark rgb(26,18,6) on dark translucent clay effective bg rgb(46,41,36), measured 1.29:1. The border remains neutral rgb(42,58,60), not clay, so the column is both low-contrast and not a clay-highlighted/double-border treatment.

Some intended filled primary buttons render transparent/flat in dark mode despite high text contrast: dashboard Upload a statement, statement Ask, and Ask Wayly about this all computed background rgba(0,0,0,0) while using bg-primary-k classes.
The 'Relevant here' pill in the Your Rights panel is dark text rgb(26,18,6) on dark surface rgb(21,36,37), measured 1.16:1, so the carried-over Your Rights legibility issue is not fully fixed.

issues: Savings/extra-cost banners and per-quarter deltas update correctly when moving Spending pace to -30/+30 in both themes.
However the adjusted column's highlight/badge treatment is not visually or contrast-safe in both themes.

action_items: Fix BudgetScenarios adjusted column classes: replace undefined bg-clay/border-clay/ring-clay with defined Wayly clay utilities or explicit CSS; ensure the What-If badge has a real clay fill and >=4.5:1 contrast in light mode.
Fix dark-mode BudgetScenarios so bg-clay/10 containers do not receive dark foreground text; adjusted column text must be readable while retaining a clay tint/border.
Fix the dark primary/accent CSS selectors so solid bg-primary-k elements with hover:bg-primary-k/90 still get a visible fill/border, not transparent/flat.
Fix the Statement Rights 'Relevant here' pill contrast; do not apply dark text to bg-terracotta/10 when the actual computed background is transparent/dark, or provide a real light pill fill.
critical_code_review_comments: BudgetScenarios.jsx uses bg-clay, border-clay, ring-clay, and bg-clay/10, but tailwind.config.js defines wayly-clay-* rather than a clay color alias; computed light-mode styles are transparent/neutral instead of clay.

index.css dark contrast pass 2 includes [class*='bg-clay/']:not(button):not(a):not([role='button']) { color:#1A1206 }, which applies to the entire adjusted projection column and causes 1.29:1 dark-mode text contrast.
index.css light-accent chip rule also catches bg-terracotta/10 pills like Statement Rights 'Relevant here', causing dark text on a dark/transparent background in dark mode.

The solid accent selector :not([class*='bg-primary-k/']) can exclude solid bg-primary-k elements that also include hover:bg-primary-k/90, leaving some intended filled buttons transparent in dark mode.

success_rate.frontend: 14/19 focused checks passed (74%); verdict not_fixed because high-priority user-visible contrast/highlight issues remain.
